subject.title: Bug: Built-in dreaming system contaminates agent identity in multi-agent setups

question: Should shared-workspace memory-core dreaming be isolated per agent by default, with any cross-agent pooling allowed only through an explicit reviewed configuration or migration path?
rationale: The current behavior crosses a memory/session privacy boundary, and the available fix paths touch plugin config, SDK helpers, persisted derived artifacts, and security review scope.

options.title: Default to per-agent isolation
options.body: Treat same-workspace cross-agent dreaming as a bug and require the fix to preserve agent boundaries through ingestion, recall, ranking, promotion, and cleanup.

options.title: Allow explicit workspace pooling
options.body: Keep workspace-level pooling only behind a documented opt-in contract with tests, warning text, and repair behavior for existing artifacts.

options.title: Defer to broader memory isolation work
options.body: Pause this issue until the broader memory/file isolation design is ready, accepting that the current dreaming bug remains open meanwhile.

recommendation.title: Default to per-agent isolation
recommendation.body: Treat same-workspace cross-agent dreaming as a bug and require the fix to preserve agent boundaries through ingestion, recall, ranking, promotion, and cleanup.

likelyOwner.reason: They are assigned on the issue and already narrowed the security-sensitive behavior question in the discussion.
